attackPath: A stale delete request could remove a newly edited API key or role because generic DELETE matched only ID. Concurrent deletes could also both report success and append duplicate audits.
rootCause: No client version requirement or atomic version predicate on deletion.
impact: Loss of newer credential/permission records, ambiguous deletion success and duplicate audit claims. Actual historical exploitation UNKNOWN.
repair: Require a valid client version, reject stale versions and atomically delete matching id/version; append audit only after one confirmed deletion.
negativeTests: 20 concurrent update/delete attempts have one success; surviving update retains version 2
Exactly one audit for the winning mutation

evidence.realLocalMongo: tmp/mongo-reliability/admin-delete-version-mongo-current.log exit 0; synthetic replica set and persisted readback; daemon/files removed

remainingLimitations: Older generic-delete callers omitting version receive 422
Webhook deletion uses a different path and last-webhook concurrency remains unresolved
Deletion/audit are still separate writes with a crash gap
Replay after successful deletion returns 404; no durable operation replay receipt
